symptomChecker.title: Pet Health Symptom Triage
symptomChecker.tagline: Answer a few guided clinical questions to assess your dog's urgency level.
symptomChecker.disclaimer: This tool provides triage guidance and care prioritization only. It is NOT a medical diagnosis and cannot replace an in-person clinical examination by a licensed veterinarian.

redFlags.label: Severe difficulty breathing, rapid shallow gasping, or persistent choking
Sudden collapse, loss of consciousness, or inability to stand
Active seizures, continuous tremors, or sudden neurological disorientation
Known or suspected ingestion of poisons (chocolate, rat poison, lilies, human medication, insecticides)
Hit by vehicle, major fall, dog attack, or acute physical trauma
Severe or continuous arterial bleeding that does not stop with light pressure
Hard, distended swollen belly with unproductive retching / dry heaving (suspected GDV)
Pale white, blue, purple, or brick-red gum discoloration
Straining repeatedly without passing any urine (urinary blockage)
Suspected venomous snake bite or rapid facial swelling from insect anaphylaxis
Severe heatstroke symptoms (excessive panting, thick drool, glazed eyes, elevated body temp)

questions.title: Symptom Duration
questions.prompt: How long have you noticed these abnormal symptoms?

questions.title: Appetite & Hydration
questions.prompt: Is your dog eating and drinking water normally?

options.label: Eating less than usual, but still drinking water
Refusing all food and water for 24+ hours

questions.title: Vomiting & Bowel Movements
questions.prompt: Are there any signs of vomiting, diarrhea, or digestive distress?

options.label: 1 or 2 mild episodes, but alert otherwise
Repeated vomiting or watery diarrhea (>3 times today)
Vomit contains blood / coffee-ground specks or black tarry stools

questions.title: Energy & Alertness Level
questions.prompt: How would you describe your dog's activity and alertness?

options.label: Bright, alert, wagging tail, and responsive
Significantly lethargic, weak, and reluctant to move

questions.title: Pain, Limping & Discomfort
questions.prompt: Does your dog show signs of pain, limping, or vocalizing when touched?

options.label: Mild limp or stiffness, still bearing weight
Cannot bear weight on a leg, whimpering, or shivering from pain

questions.title: Companion Age Group
questions.prompt: What is your dog's current life stage?

emergency.title: Immediate Emergency Clinic Visit Needed
emergency.subtitle: Your pet exhibits symptoms that can be life-threatening if delayed. Please proceed to Bastet Emergency Hospital immediately.
guidance: Keep your pet calm and warm during transport. Limit movement as much as possible.
If poisoning is suspected, bring the packaging, chemical container, or plant sample with you.
Do NOT force feed, induce vomiting, or apply tourniquets without direct veterinary instruction.
Do NOT administer human painkillers (paracetamol, ibuprofen, and aspirin are highly toxic to dogs).

today.title: Same-Day Veterinary Examination Recommended
today.subtitle: Your pet should be evaluated by a veterinarian within the next 12 to 24 hours to prevent complications.
guidance: Offer small, controlled sips of fresh water at room temperature. Avoid large gulps.
Rest in a quiet, comfortable indoor space away from stairs, draft, or direct heat.
Record short videos of abnormal behavior or posture to show the clinical doctor.
If your pet collapses or breathing becomes labored, proceed immediately to the emergency line.

soon.title: Outpatient Veterinary Consultation Recommended
soon.subtitle: Schedule an examination within 1 to 3 days for diagnostic workup and targeted treatment.
guidance: Maintain their standard balanced diet; avoid introducing sudden new foods or table scraps.
Limit strenuous exercise, high jumps, or prolonged outdoor walks until examined.
Check temperature, appetite, and stool consistency twice daily and note any changes.

monitor.title: At-Home Observation & Care
monitor.subtitle: Symptoms appear mild at this stage. Keep a close watch over your companion at home over the next 24 to 48 hours.
guidance: Ensure constant access to fresh, clean drinking water and a quiet resting spot.
Maintain their regular feeding routine without heavy treats or rich foods.
If symptoms worsen, new signs emerge, or distress continues past 48 hours, consult a veterinarian promptly.
